original_value: AbstractSomatic mutation and gene expression dysregulation are considered two major tumorigenesis factors. While independent investigations of either factor pervade, studies of associations between somatic mutations and gene expression changes have been sporadic and nonsystematic. Utilizing genomic data collected from 11 315 subjects of 33 distinct cancer types, we constructed MutEx, a pan-cancer integrative genomic database. This database records the relationships among gene expression, somatic mutation and survival data for cancer patients. MutEx can be used to swiftly explore the relationship between these genomic/clinic features within and across cancer types and, more importantly, search for corroborating evidence for hypothesis inception. Our database also incorporated Gene Ontology and several pathway databases to enhance functional annotation, and elastic net and a gene expression composite score to aid in survival analysis. To demonstrate the usability of MutEx, we provide several application examples, including top somatic mutations associated with the most extensive expression dysregulation in breast cancer, differential mutational burden downstream of DNA mismatch repair gene mutations and composite gene expression score-based survival difference in breast cancer. MutEx can be accessed at http://www.innovebioinfo.com/Databases/Mutationdb_About.php.

result.paraphrase: Somatic mutations and abnormal gene expression are regarded as two key drivers of tumorigenesis. Although each has been widely studied on its own, research on links between somatic mutations and expression changes has been limited and uneven. Using genomic data from 11 315 subjects across 33 cancer types, we developed MutEx, a pan-cancer integrative genomic database. It captures relationships among gene expression, somatic mutation, and survival data for cancer patients. MutEx enables rapid exploration of these genomic and clinical features within and across cancer types and, importantly, helps identify corroborating evidence for hypothesis generation. The database also integrates Gene Ontology and multiple pathway databases for improved functional annotation, and includes elastic net plus a gene expression composite score to support survival analysis. To illustrate MutEx’s utility, we present several examples, including the top somatic mutations linked to the greatest expression dysregulation in breast cancer, differential mutational burden downstream of DNA mismatch repair gene mutations, and survival differences in breast cancer based on the composite gene expression score. MutEx is available at http://www.innovebioinfo.com/Databases/Mutationdb_About.php.
